instruction: Use ANSYS Fluent to complete a 3D laminar pipe-flow analysis. Physical problem: Steady laminar flow of water through a straight circular pipe. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use a 3D model. - Use SI units in Fluent. - The pipe axis is along the global X direction. - The pipe length is 100 mm, equivalent to 0.100 m. - The pipe diameter is 4 mm, equivalent to 0.004 m. - The pipe radius is 0.002 m. - The circular cross-section is centered on the X axis: - Cross-section center: Y = 0 m, Z = 0 m - Radius: 0.002 m - The pipe domain should extend from: - X = 0 m at the inlet - X = 0.100 m at the outlet Boundary zone names: - Name the inlet boundary: inlet - Name the outlet boundary: outlet - Name the pipe wall boundary: wall Model parameters: - Fluid: water - Use constant material properties: - Density: 998.2 kg/m³ - Dynamic viscosity: 0.001003 Pa·s - Mesh: - Use a structured hexahedral or swept mesh. - Include 3 boundary-layer layers near the pipe wall. - Use sufficient axial and radial resolution to resolve the laminar velocity profile. Boundary conditions: - Inlet: - Velocity inlet - Mean inlet velocity = 0.1 m/s in the positive X direction - Outlet: - Pressure outlet - Gauge pressure = 0 Pa - Pipe wall: - Stationary no-slip wall Solver setup: - Solver type: pressure-based - Time setting: steady - Flow model: laminar - Pressure-velocity coupling: SIMPLE - Spatial discretization: second-order schemes where applicable - Initialize the solution and iterate until convergence. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the working directory. - Save the Fluent case file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\pipe_laminar.cas - Save the Fluent data file as: C:\Users\user\Desktop\pipe_laminar.dat Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated.
